Ray Diagrams to Predict Images

Imaging the tip of a pencil:

__Ray 1 __ makes an incident angle of 0°\, therefore reflected angle is 0 __°__ __Ray 2 __ makes an incident angle of θ°\, therefore reflected angle is __θ’__ __°__

Both rays can be traced back to their point of apparent origination behind the mirror

Imaging the tip of a pencil:

Dashed lines behind the mirror meet at the image point \, or where the image appears to be

The collection of all of these rays forms the virtual image

The virtual image appears as far behind the mirror as the pencil is in front of it

( p = q)

Ray Diagrams on Flat Mirrors

Imaging the tip of a pencil:

Dashed lines behind the mirror meet at the image point \, or where the image appears to be

The collection of all of these rays forms the virtual image

The virtual image appears as far behind the mirror as the pencil is in front of it

( p = q)

Images on Flat Mirrors

Images in flat mirrors appear reversed to an observer in front of the mirror

Angles of perspective are maintained

Images on Curved Mirrors

Images formed on curved mirrors are rather different from those on flat mirrors

Dashed lines behind the mirror meet at the image point \, or where the image appears to be

The collection of all of these rays forms the virtual image

The virtual image appears as far behind the mirror as the pencil is in front of it

( p = q)

Example 1 | A pendulum clock

A pendulum clock is being designed to have a period of exactly 1.0 s. How long should the pendulum be?

Holt, Sample B, Q2
25 cm

Example 2 | Suspension on a car

The body of a 1 275 kg car is supported on a frame by four springs. Two people riding in the car have a combined mass of 153 kg. When driven over a pothole in the road\, the frame vibrates with a period of 0.840 s. For the first few seconds\, the vibration approximates SHM. Find the spring constant of the suspension springs.

Holt, Sample C, pp. 380
2.00 x 10⁴ N/m each

Example 3 | A piano string

A piano string tuned to middle C vibrates with a frequency of 262 Hz. Assuming the speed of sound in air is 343 m/s\, find the wavelength of the sound waves produced by the string.

Holt, Sample D, p. 387

Wavelength = 1.31 m
